executive_summary: A grounded AI assistant for university course documents, helping students query lectures, slides, and syllabus with high precision citations.
objectives: Answer course questions accurately with citations from lecture PDFs
Ensure sub-second search and answer latency for classroom use
Operate within a restricted GPU/hosting budget
technical_architecture:
## System Architecture

The architecture relies on a modern RAG pipeline:
- **Ingestion**: PDFs parsed using PyPDFium2 and chunked with RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter.
- **Embedding**: Dense embeddings generated using text-embedding-3-small.
- **Vector Store**: ChromaDB running locally for metadata-filtered retrieval.
- **Orchestration**: LangGraph state graph routing user queries with feedback loops.
dataset_plan: Collect official lecture slides and course notes. Cross-reference with standard benchmarks.
dataset_discovery_note: Recommended datasets sourced from Hugging Face and academic archives.

dataset_recommendations.name: rajpurkar/squad
dataset_recommendations.description: Stanford Question Answering Dataset benchmark for reading comprehension.
dataset_recommendations.relevance: Used to validate question-answering capabilities before deploying course materials.

model_plan: Deploy Gemini 2.0 Flash or gemini-3.5-flash-lite as the generation LLM, paired with local ChromaDB vectors.
implementation_roadmap: Phase 1: Ingest course syllabus and slide decks into ChromaDB
Phase 2: Build FastAPI endpoints for semantic search and question answering
Phase 3: Deploy Next.js student portal and test grounding accuracy
risks_and_mitigations: Hallucination on technical formulas: Mitigate with strict citation thresholds and prompt guardrails
Outdated course material: Implement scheduled re-indexing when professors update slides
